# nonFunctionLike

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is **not** callable.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonFunctionLike() — Checks whether a value is **not** callable. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonFunctionLike<T>(value: T | Function): value is T;
```

`nonFunctionLike(value)` is the same test as `!isFunctionLike(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

The cheap test — `typeof value === "function"` — which is what you want before calling something. `isFunction` is the stricter reading of the same question.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type            | Description         |
| :-------- | :-------------- | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `T \| Function` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is not callable; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `T` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
nonFunctionLike(null); // => true
nonFunctionLike({}); // => true
nonFunctionLike("fn"); // => true
nonFunctionLike(function () {}); // => false
nonFunctionLike(Math.max); // => false
```
